title: The coder loop: dry-run first, then the compile-gated fix — free, anonymous, entirely on your machine
intro: Press play to walk the flow one step at a time, or click a dot to jump.

walk.title: Install
walk.text: One prebuilt binary (Homebrew, Scoop, the install script, or `cargo install cargo-refine`) lands in ~/.cargo/bin — no repo clone, no build. It stays anonymous: fixing needs no account.

walk.title: Dry run first
walk.text: The bare `cargo refine` is a review: it lists the fixes it would make across your crate and writes nothing. No listing is published as a fixture — your code never leaves the machine, so this walk shows real bytes only where a step crosses to the network.

walk.title: The compile gate
walk.text: `cargo refine fix` writes an edit only if your crate still compiles after it; a breaking fix is reverted automatically. Divergence classes the gate cannot judge (comment-guarded matches, array-literal defaults) stay manual and are listed, not applied.

walk.title: What you get
walk.text: Healed code across the shipped domains — clippy lints, compile errors, Rust perf, Dockerfiles, release profiles — plus the local self-evolve loop: memory always records, learning runs when the oracle is present. Hosted lanes, where a deployment funds them, are metered by contribution points as fair use — never local healing.
